Users resource: invite, update and deactivate
chunks.doc_title: Nimbus Gateway REST API v2 reference
chunks.heading: Users resource: invite, update and deactivate
chunks.text: Deactivation removes the person's ability to sign in without erasing their account history. Before you do this, reassign any content they own so that nobody loses access to important work. You can reactivate the account later if the person returns.

chunks.heading: What's new in Nimbus Sync
chunks.text: This release introduces a new sync engine, rebuilt to make the first sync of a workspace noticeably faster. If you connect a new device or add a large folder for the first time, you should see files begin to appear sooner, and the progress indicator in the Nimbus Sync menu bar panel will move along more smoothly. The new engine is available on the Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans, and no setup is required. Nimbus Sync updates automatically, so simply restart the app if it prompts you, then let the initial sync run as usual.

chunks.heading: What's new in Nimbus Sync
chunks.text: Known issue: Pro users who sign in with SSO may see error E4012 after the laptop wakes from sleep. If this happens, open the Nimbus Sync panel, sign in again through your identity provider, and choose Resume sync. We are investigating and will share an update as soon as a fix is ready.

chunks.heading: Known issue: E4012 after wake from sleep
chunks.text:
This release includes a mitigation for error E4012, which some Pro and Enterprise users saw when a laptop resumed from sleep. Previously the Nimbus Sync client could wake with an expired session token, and the first sync attempt would fail with E4012 and a red banner in the status panel. Now the client detects the failed authentication and retries the token refresh automatically, so in most cases the sync resumes without any action from you. If you still see the banner after waking your device, try this:
1. Open the Nimbus Sync menu and select Sync status. 2. Choose Retry now. 3. If E4012 persists, sign out and sign back in. The root cause is still under investigation, and we will share more details once it is understood.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Sync 5.2: token refresh fix and Sync health panel
chunks.text:
Nimbus Sync 5.2 is available today for Pro workspaces. This release addresses a problem that interrupted sync for some customers. Fixed: we found and fixed the root cause of E4012 for Pro users. Previously, the client could try to use an access token that was about to lapse, especially on devices whose clocks had drifted. The client now refreshes tokens 10 minutes before they expire and tolerates up to 15 minutes of clock skew, so sync should continue without asking you to sign in again. New: we added a Sync health panel. To open it:
1. Open Nimbus Sync and go to Preferences. 2. Select Health. 3. Review the panel for the current state of your sync connection. If you still see E4012 after updating, restart the client once so it picks up the new refresh behavior, then contact support.

chunks.heading: Fixes in this release
chunks.text: This maintenance release of Nimbus Sync addresses a stability problem reported by Mac users and is available on the Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans. Fixed a crash on macOS 15 when renaming a folder during sync. Previously, if you changed the name of a folder while Nimbus Sync was still transferring files inside it, the desktop app could quit unexpectedly. The app now handles the rename cleanly, and the sync continues without interruption. For example, say you are syncing a project folder called "Q3 Drafts" and rename it to "Q3 Final" in Finder while uploads are in progress.

chunks.heading: Fixes in this release
chunks.text: Before this update, that sequence could trigger the crash on macOS 15. With this release, the rename completes and the sync carries on as expected. No configuration changes are needed. We recommend that everyone running Nimbus Sync on macOS 15 update to this release as soon as it is convenient.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Sync 5.3: clearer Free workspace messages and Ubuntu 24.04 packages
chunks.text: Nimbus Sync 5.3 brings two practical improvements for teams on the Free plan. First, when a workspace goes over the Free user limit, devices that belong to that workspace now show a clear message in the Sync window instead of the cryptic E4012 error. The message explains that the workspace has more users than the Free plan allows and points the workspace owner to the billing page, where they can remove users or review plan options. Other members see a short note asking them to contact their owner. Syncing resumes as soon as the workspace is back within its allowance, with no need to sign out or reinstall.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Sync 5.3: clearer Free workspace messages and Ubuntu 24.04 packages
chunks.text: Second, we have added Ubuntu 24.04 packages, so you can install Nimbus Sync with your usual package manager and receive updates the same way as on other supported systems. To upgrade, open the Sync menu, choose About, and select Check for updates.

chunks.heading: Per-plan burst limits
chunks.text: This release of Nimbus Gateway introduces per-plan burst limits for Starter, Pro, and Enterprise workspaces. A burst limit caps how many requests a client can send in a short spike, so one noisy integration no longer crowds out the rest of your traffic. Each plan now has its own burst limit, and you can see the limit that applies to your workspace under Settings > Gateway > Traffic. When a client goes over its burst limit, Gateway rejects the request with HTTP 429 and the error code E4290. The response also includes a Retry-After header telling the client how long to wait before trying again.

chunks.heading: Per-plan burst limits
chunks.text: We recommend that your clients read this header and back off accordingly, rather than retrying immediately. If you see E4290 often in your request logs, spread calls out more evenly or review which plan fits your traffic.

chunks.heading: Gateway 3.1: clearer auth failures and rotating webhook secrets
chunks.text: Nimbus Gateway 3.1 is now available to Pro and Enterprise workspaces. This release focuses on making authentication problems and webhook security easier to manage. Responses that return E4012 now include an X-Nimbus-Auth-Reason header. The header tells you whether the token expired or was revoked. Previously, clients had to guess which case they were in. Now an expired token can trigger a normal refresh, while a revoked token can send the user back to sign in. You can read the header in your client code or check it in your request logs. Webhook signatures can now use a second, rotating secret.

chunks.heading: Gateway 3.1: clearer auth failures and rotating webhook secrets
chunks.text:
This lets you replace a signing secret without interrupting delivery:

1. Add the new secret alongside the current one in your webhook settings. 2. Update your receiving service so it accepts either secret. 3. Once traffic is verified, retire the old secret. No changes are required if you keep your existing setup.

chunks.heading: APAC (Tokyo) regional endpoint now generally available
chunks.text:
The APAC (Tokyo) regional endpoint, api.apac.nimbus.example, is now generally available for Nimbus Gateway on the Enterprise plan. Teams with users and services in Asia-Pacific can send traffic to this endpoint instead of routing requests through a distant region. To start using it:

1. Sign in to the Nimbus Gateway console and open the Endpoints view. 2. Find the APAC (Tokyo) entry in the regional endpoint list and review its status. 3. Update your client configuration or environment variables so the base URL points to api.apac.nimbus.example. 4. Send a test request and confirm it returns a successful response before moving production traffic.

chunks.heading: APAC (Tokyo) regional endpoint now generally available
chunks.text: We recommend switching one service at a time, so you can compare behavior and roll back by restoring your previous base URL if needed. Your existing endpoints keep working, and no changes are required for workloads that don't need the new region. Contact your Nimbus account team with any questions about rollout planning.

chunks.heading: New in Nimbus Analytics 2.3: BigQuery connector
chunks.text: Nimbus Analytics 2.3 adds the BigQuery data source connector, so teams that keep their warehouse data in Google Cloud can now bring it straight into Nimbus Analytics. The connector is available on the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans. To set it up, open Data Sources from the left navigation and select Add data source. BigQuery now appears in the list of available connectors alongside the existing options. Choose it, give the connection a recognizable name, and enter the details for your Google Cloud project when prompted. Select Test connection to confirm that Nimbus Analytics can reach your project, then save.

chunks.heading: New in Nimbus Analytics 2.3: BigQuery connector
chunks.text: Once the connection is saved, your BigQuery tables can be selected when you build a new dataset. From there they work like any other source, so you can use them in explorations and dashboards. For example, an analyst could connect a marketing events table and chart campaign activity next to data from other connected sources without exporting files first.

chunks.heading: Higher dashboard widget limit for Pro
chunks.text:
This release raises the Pro dashboard widget limit from 25 to 40, giving teams more room to build detailed dashboards without splitting related metrics across separate views. The change applies to every existing Pro workspace automatically, so you don't need to update settings or contact support. To take advantage of it, open any dashboard in Nimbus Analytics and select Edit in the upper right corner. Then:

1. Choose Add widget from the toolbar. 2. Pick a chart type and the data source you want to visualize. 3. Select Save to place the widget on the canvas.

chunks.heading: Higher dashboard widget limit for Pro
chunks.text: If a dashboard was previously full, the Add widget button will now be available again until it reaches the new limit. Your existing dashboards, layouts, filters, and sharing settings stay exactly as they were. We recommend grouping related widgets under clear section headings so larger dashboards remain easy to scan for everyone who views them.

chunks.heading: Faster refresh and PDF export for Enterprise dashboards
chunks.text:
This release brings two improvements to Nimbus Analytics for Enterprise workspaces. First, Enterprise dashboards now refresh every minute instead of every 5 minutes, so the charts and tables your teams watch stay closer to the underlying data. You don't need to change any settings. Existing dashboards pick up the new refresh cadence automatically, and anyone with a dashboard open will see the more frequent updates. Second, we added PDF export for dashboards. To share a dashboard outside Nimbus, follow these steps:

1. Open the dashboard you want to share. 2. Select Export from the dashboard toolbar. 3. Choose PDF. 4. Save the generated file when your browser prompts you. The PDF reflects the dashboard as it appears when you export it, which makes it handy for review meetings, status reports, and sending a snapshot to colleagues who don't have a Nimbus login.

chunks.heading: Passkeys for two-factor authentication
chunks.text:
Starting with the August 2026 release of Nimbus Platform, passkeys can now be used for two-factor authentication on all plans, including Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise. Until now, passkeys were not available as a second factor, so teams relied on authenticator apps or other existing methods. With this update, you can use the fingerprint, face recognition, or device PIN you already trust on your laptop or phone. To set one up, follow these steps:

1. Open your profile menu and choose Security. 2. Under Two-factor authentication, select Add a method. 3. Choose Passkey and follow the prompt from your browser or device. 4.

chunks.heading: Passkeys for two-factor authentication
chunks.text: Give the passkey a recognizable name, such as "Work laptop," and confirm. The next time you sign in, Nimbus will ask you to verify with your passkey after you enter your password. Your existing two-factor methods remain available as alternatives, so you can switch between them whenever you need to.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Platform October 2026 release: Enterprise compliance updates
chunks.text: This October release brings two compliance improvements to Nimbus Platform for Enterprise customers, aimed at teams that handle discovery requests and regular audits. Legal holds on shared drives. Until now, administrators had to place legal holds one file at a time. You can now place a hold on a whole shared drive, so everything stored there is preserved while the matter is open. To use it, open the Admin console, choose Legal holds, select Create hold, and pick Shared drive as the scope. Choose the drive, add a matter name, and confirm. Individual file holds still work the same way and can be used alongside drive-level holds.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Platform October 2026 release: Enterprise compliance updates
chunks.text: Daily audit log export to Amazon S3. Audit logs can now be exported daily to an Amazon S3 bucket that you own. Under Security settings, open Audit exports, enter your bucket details, and turn on the daily schedule. This makes it easier to feed logs into your existing archive or monitoring tools. Both features are available to Enterprise workspace administrators.

chunks.heading: Security and collaboration updates
chunks.text: This month's Nimbus Platform release focuses on how people sign in and who you can invite to work with you. Guest access is now available on the Starter plan. Teams on Starter can bring in outside collaborators, such as contractors or clients, without giving them full member accounts. Workspace admins can invite a guest by email, and guests see only what has been shared with them. Pro and Enterprise customers already have guest access, and nothing changes for them. We are also announcing a change to two-factor authentication. SMS codes for two-factor authentication will be removed on March 31, 2027.

chunks.heading: Security and collaboration updates
chunks.text:
If you currently receive codes by text message, switch to an authenticator app or passkeys before then so you keep access to your account. To switch, follow these steps:

1. Open your account security settings. 2. Add an authenticator app or a passkey. 3. Remove SMS as a verification method. Admins may want to remind their teams to make this change early.

chunks.doc_title: What happens when I downgrade from Pro to Starter?
chunks.heading: What happens when I downgrade from Pro to Starter?
chunks.text: Downgrading from Pro to Starter in Nimbus Platform changes a few things, so it helps to know what to expect before you confirm. To start, open Settings, choose Billing, select Change plan, and pick Starter. You'll see a summary screen before anything is final. Single sign-on turns off at the end of the current billing period, and users must set a password to keep signing in. We recommend asking your team to watch for the password email so nobody is locked out. Audit logs stay available read-only for 90 days after the downgrade, so you can still review and export past activity during that time.

chunks.doc_title: What happens when I downgrade from Pro to Starter?
chunks.heading: What happens when I downgrade from Pro to Starter?
chunks.text: If your workspace holds more data than Starter allows, your files over Starter storage remain available, but no new uploads are possible until usage is under the limit. Deleting or archiving old files from the Files page is the quickest way to get back under it.

chunks.heading: Refund policy for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text:
This article explains when you can get money back for a Nimbus Platform subscription on the Starter, Pro, or Enterprise plan. Annual plans can be refunded pro rata within 30 days of purchase or renewal. Pro rata means you are charged only for the time you actually used, and the unused remainder of the term is returned to your original payment method. Monthly plans are not refundable, so if you cancel a monthly subscription, it simply stays active until the end of the current billing period and does not renew. To request an annual refund, follow these steps:
1. Sign in as an account owner or billing admin. 2.

chunks.heading: Refund policy for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text: Open Settings, then Billing. 3. Check the purchase or renewal date shown under your current plan, and make sure the request falls within the 30-day window. 4. Select Contact support and tell us you would like an annual plan refund.

chunks.heading: Cancelling a Nimbus subscription
chunks.text: If you no longer need Nimbus Platform, workspace owners can cancel a Starter, Pro, or Enterprise subscription at any time. To begin, sign in and open Settings, then choose Billing. Select Cancel subscription, pick the reason that best fits your situation, and confirm when prompted. You will see a confirmation banner at the top of the Billing screen once the request has gone through. It helps to know what happens next. After cancellation the workspace becomes read-only, so your team can still view projects and records but cannot add or change anything.

chunks.heading: Cancelling a Nimbus subscription
chunks.text: Your data is kept for 30 days before it is deleted, which gives you time to decide whether you want to keep a copy. During those 30 days, owners can export all data under Settings > Export. Choose what you want to include, start the export, and download the file when it is ready. We recommend doing this before the retention window closes, since deleted data cannot be recovered.

chunks.doc_title: My Free workspace has more than 3 users
chunks.heading: My Free workspace has more than 3 users
chunks.text: If your Free workspace has more than 3 users, you may notice that some teammates can no longer edit. Since September 15, 2026, Free workspaces with more than 3 users keep working for the first 3 users by join date. Everyone else in the workspace gets read-only access until the workspace upgrades or removes users. For example, if five people belong to your workspace, the three who joined earliest continue as normal, while the two most recent members can view content but not change it.

chunks.doc_title: My Free workspace has more than 3 users
chunks.heading: My Free workspace has more than 3 users
chunks.text:
When affected users open Nimbus Sync, they see a message explaining the limit, so they know why editing is unavailable and that it is not a sync error. To restore access for everyone, you have two options:
1. Open Settings, then Billing, and choose a paid plan such as Starter or Pro. 2. Open Settings, then Members, and remove users you no longer need. Only workspace owners and admins can make these changes.

chunks.heading: Payment methods for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text:
Nimbus Platform supports several ways to pay, depending on your plan and billing setup. Credit and debit cards are accepted on all paid plans, so Starter, Pro, and Enterprise customers can always pay by card. ACH bank transfer is available for annual Pro and Enterprise plans billed in US dollars. If your account is billed monthly or in another currency, ACH will not appear as an option. Enterprise customers can also pay by invoice with 30-day terms, which suits teams that route payments through an accounts payable process. To update your payment method:
1. Sign in and open Settings, then select Billing. 2. Choose Payment method and click Change. 3.

chunks.heading: Payment methods for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text: Select Card, ACH, or Invoice, depending on what your plan offers. 4. Enter the details and click Save. If an option is missing, check your plan and billing currency first. Billing admins can make these changes.

chunks.heading: Adding and removing seats
chunks.text: You can change the number of seats on your Nimbus Platform subscription at any time if you are on the Starter, Pro, or Enterprise plan. You need to be an account owner or billing admin to make the change. To add or remove seats, open Settings, choose Billing, and select Manage seats. Enter the new total number of seats and review the summary shown before you confirm. When you add seats, they are available to assign right away. Added seats are charged pro rata for the rest of the billing period, so you only pay for the time they are active in your current cycle.

chunks.heading: Adding and removing seats
chunks.text: When you reduce seats, remove the affected users first, or choose which users to deactivate during the change. Removed seats are credited at the next renewal, not refunded. The credit appears as a line item on your next invoice and lowers the amount due. If you have questions about a specific invoice, contact our support team from the Help menu.

chunks.heading: Nonprofit and education discounts
chunks.text: Nimbus Platform offers discounted pricing to qualifying nonprofits and schools on the Starter and Pro plans. Here is how each type of organization applies. Nonprofits: sign in as an account owner or billing admin and open Settings > Billing > Discounts. Select the nonprofit option and enter your organization's details. We verify nonprofit status through TechSoup, so you may be asked to confirm your TechSoup validation during the process. Once your status is approved, the discount applies from the next invoice. Invoices that have already been issued are not changed. Schools: educational institutions apply with proof of accreditation.

chunks.heading: Nonprofit and education discounts
chunks.text: Submit the request from the same Discounts screen and attach documentation showing that your school is accredited. Our team reviews it and notifies the billing contact by email when a decision is made. If your application is not approved, check that the organization name matches your records and that the documents are legible, then submit again.

chunks.heading: Changing the billing owner
chunks.text: The billing owner is the person who receives invoices, manages the payment method, and can change the subscription for your Nimbus Platform workspace. If that person is leaving your company or handing off finance duties, you can move the role to a colleague. Only the current Owner can transfer billing ownership, so make sure you are signed in with the Owner account before you begin. Admins and other roles will not see the transfer option. Before you start, confirm that your chosen colleague already has the Admin role.

chunks.heading: Changing the billing owner
chunks.text: The new owner must already be an Admin, so if they are a Member or Viewer, promote them first from the Users list. 1. Go to Settings > Billing > Owner. 2. Choose the Admin you want from the list. 3. Review the confirmation message and select Transfer ownership. The new owner will be notified by email and will see the Billing section the next time they sign in. This applies to the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans.

chunks.heading: Deleting a user account
chunks.text: Admins can remove people from a Nimbus Platform workspace when they leave a team or no longer need access. To delete a user, open Admin Console, select Users, and find the person in the list. Click the three-dot menu at the end of their row, choose Delete user, and confirm in the dialog that appears. Before you confirm, it helps to know what happens to the user's content. When an admin deletes a user, the user's files move to the admin who deleted them. For example, if Priya deletes Marcus's account, Marcus's files will appear in Priya's file library, and she can then reassign or share them as needed.

chunks.heading: Deleting a user account
chunks.text: If you delete someone by mistake, you don't need to start over. Deleted users can be restored for 20 days. To bring an account back, go to Users, open the Deleted tab, and select Restore next to the person's name. This applies to every plan, including Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise.

chunks.doc_title: What happens when storage is full?
chunks.heading: What happens when storage is full?
chunks.text:
When your account reaches its storage limit, new uploads stop working, but nothing you have already stored is touched. Existing files stay available, so you can still open, preview, and download them as usual. How the problem appears depends on where the space ran out. If your cloud quota is full, you will see a 'storage full' banner at the top of the Nimbus Platform dashboard. If the local disk on your computer is full, Nimbus Sync shows error E1001 instead. The error code appears only for a full local disk, so a full cloud quota will not trigger it. To get uploads working again:
1.

chunks.doc_title: What happens when storage is full?
chunks.heading: What happens when storage is full?
chunks.text: Check which message you are seeing. 2. For the banner, delete files you no longer need or review your plan under Billing. 3. For E1001, free up space on your computer and let Nimbus Sync retry. Uploads that failed will not resume on their own in the browser, so add those files again once space is available.

chunks.heading: Enterprise uptime commitment and service credits
chunks.text: This Service Level Agreement describes the availability Nimbus commits to for Nimbus Gateway and the remedies available when we fall short. This section covers customers on the Enterprise plan. For Enterprise customers, Nimbus commits to 99.95% monthly uptime for Nimbus Gateway. Uptime is assessed across each calendar month, so a poor stretch in one month does not carry over into the next, and a strong month does not offset a weak one. If Gateway availability in a month falls short of that commitment, you are entitled to a service credit.

chunks.heading: Enterprise uptime commitment and service credits
chunks.text:
The credit is calculated as a percentage of the monthly Gateway fee you pay, and the size of the credit increases with the severity of the shortfall:

- If uptime is below 99.95%, the credit is 10% of the monthly Gateway fee.
- If uptime is below 99.0%, the credit is 25% of the monthly Gateway fee.
- If uptime is below 95.0%, the credit is 50% of the monthly Gateway fee. The tiers do not stack. Only the highest tier that applies to a given month is used.

chunks.heading: Enterprise uptime commitment and service credits
chunks.text: For example, if a month ends with uptime below 99.0% but not below 95.0%, the credit is 25% of that month's Gateway fee, not 25% plus 10%. Service credits are the remedy for missing the uptime commitment. They are calculated only against the Gateway fee, not against other Nimbus products you may use, such as Nimbus Platform, Nimbus Sync, or Nimbus Analytics.

chunks.heading: Pro coverage, exclusions and how to claim credits
chunks.text:
Nimbus Gateway customers on the Pro plan are also covered by an uptime commitment. For Pro, Nimbus commits to 99.9% monthly uptime. If uptime in a month is below 99.9%, a 10% credit applies to the monthly Gateway fee. Pro has a single credit tier, so there are no higher levels of credit for a deeper shortfall. The Free and Starter plans have no SLA. No uptime commitment or service credit applies to Gateway usage on those plans, although we still work to keep the service available for everyone. Credits are not applied automatically. To receive one, follow these steps:

1.

chunks.heading: Pro coverage, exclusions and how to claim credits
chunks.text: Sign in and open a request with Nimbus support, choosing Gateway as the product concerned. 2. State the affected month and your plan, and describe the availability problems you observed, including approximate times and any request failures your own monitoring recorded. 3. Submit the request and keep the confirmation so you can refer to it in later correspondence. You must request the credit through support within 30 days of the end of the month in which the shortfall occurred. Requests received after that window cannot be honored, so we recommend reviewing your Gateway availability at the close of each month. Support will review your request against our own uptime records and confirm the outcome with you.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Encryption of customer data
chunks.text: Protecting the data you place in Nimbus Platform starts with encryption at every stage of its life. Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256, which covers databases, file storage and backups. Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or later, so connections from browsers, the API and connected integrations are protected as they travel across networks. Older protocol versions are refused, and clients that cannot negotiate a modern connection will see a failed handshake instead of a silent downgrade. For most customers on the Free, Starter and Pro plans, encryption keys are managed by Nimbus on your behalf, so there is nothing to configure.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Encryption of customer data
chunks.text: Protection is on from the moment a workspace is created, and no setting needs to be switched on or off. Enterprise customers who need direct control over their keys can use customer-managed keys, often called bring your own key, through AWS KMS. In practice, your security team creates a key in your own AWS account, grants Nimbus permission to use it for your workspace, and then selects that key in the workspace security settings. Because the key stays in your account, you can review how it is used and revoke access if your policies require it. Revoking access makes the encrypted data unreadable to Nimbus until access is restored, so coordinate any change with your administrators before you act.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Compliance reports and certifications
chunks.text: Customers often ask for independent proof that our controls work as described, and Nimbus maintains several forms of it. We hold a SOC 2 Type II report covering April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. A Type II report is useful in a vendor review because an independent auditor tests how controls operated across the whole period, not only on a single day. We have also held ISO 27001 certification since November 2025, which confirms that our information security management system meets an internationally recognized standard.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Compliance reports and certifications
chunks.text: When you start a vendor assessment, a typical approach is to gather your questionnaire, identify which controls matter most to your organization, and compare them with the scope described in our reports. Your Nimbus account team can help you map specific questions to the relevant sections so your reviewers do not have to read every line. Organizations that handle protected health information have an additional requirement. A HIPAA business associate agreement (BAA) is available for Enterprise only. If you are on another plan and expect to process health data, talk to your account team about moving to Enterprise before any such data enters your workspace. Please do not upload protected health information until the agreement has been signed by both parties.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Testing and vulnerability reporting
chunks.text: Nimbus does not rely only on internal reviews to find weaknesses. Independent penetration tests run once a year, performed by outside specialists who attempt to break into the platform the way a real attacker might. Findings are triaged by severity, assigned to the responsible engineering team, and tracked until they are fixed and verified. Customers on Enterprise can request the summary of the most recent test through their account team. The summary is shared under confidentiality, so expect to confirm who will read it and how it will be stored. Testing by professionals is complemented by the wider research community.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Testing and vulnerability reporting
chunks.text: Nimbus runs a public bug bounty program, which invites security researchers to report vulnerabilities responsibly. If you believe you have found an issue, follow the program guidelines: describe the problem clearly, include the steps needed to reproduce it, and avoid accessing data that belongs to other customers. Please do not run tests that could degrade service for other people, and give our team reasonable time to investigate before you disclose anything publicly. Reports are reviewed by the security team, who may ask follow-up questions. Valid findings are fixed according to their impact, and researchers who follow the rules are credited as the program describes.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Access controls inside Nimbus
chunks.text: Security is not only about what outsiders can reach; it also depends on what our own staff can see. Inside Nimbus, access follows the principle of least privilege. Employees receive only the permissions needed for their current role, and those permissions are tied to individual accounts rather than shared logins. When someone changes teams or leaves the company, their access is reviewed and removed so that old permissions do not linger. Support work is handled with the same care. Our support engineers cannot browse customer workspaces at will.

briefs: Access controls inside Nimbus: least privilege for staff and logging of support access
chunks.heading: Access controls inside Nimbus
chunks.text: If a ticket requires looking at your configuration, the engineer works from the minimum information needed to resolve the problem, and access is limited to that purpose. Every instance of support access is logged, including who accessed what and when, so the activity can be reviewed later by our security team. You can help keep this process tidy. When you open a ticket, describe the problem clearly, name the affected workspace or integration, and avoid pasting passwords or secret keys into the message. If you want to know why a support engineer needed to view something, ask your account team, who can guide you through what the review covers. As a good habit, review your own workspace members regularly and remove anyone who no longer needs access, so your internal permissions reflect the same discipline we apply.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Subprocessors
chunks.text: Nimbus relies on a small group of trusted third-party subprocessors to deliver Nimbus Platform to customers on the Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans. This document describes who they are and what each one does. Amazon Web Services provides our hosting infrastructure, where Nimbus Platform runs and where customer data is stored. Stripe processes payments, including card transactions for paid plan subscriptions. Twilio delivers the SMS codes used for verification when a user signs in or confirms a sensitive change. Zendesk manages support tickets, so messages sent to our support team are handled within that system.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Subprocessors
chunks.text: Each subprocessor is bound by a written agreement that requires it to protect customer information and use it only for the service it provides to Nimbus. We keep this list current. Customers are notified 30 days before a new subprocessor is added, giving account owners time to review the change and raise questions with their Nimbus contact before it takes effect. Notices go to the primary account owner's email address, so please keep it up to date in your workspace settings.

chunks.heading: Overview and system requirements
chunks.text: This guide documents Nimbus Sync 4.x, the retired desktop client for keeping folders consistent across your devices and your Nimbus workspace. Nimbus Sync 4.x reached end of support on January 31, 2026, so it no longer receives fixes or assistance from the support team. The guide is kept for administrators who still maintain older machines and need to understand how the client behaved. Anyone starting a new rollout should use a current Nimbus Sync release instead. Before installing, confirm that your computer is supported. Nimbus Sync 4.x runs on Windows 8.1 or later and macOS 11 or later.

chunks.heading: Overview and system requirements
chunks.text:
Earlier operating systems are not supported, and the installer may refuse to launch on them. To install the client, follow these steps:

1. Download the installer package from your archived deployment location. 2. Run the installer and accept the license agreement. 3. Sign in with your Nimbus account when the welcome window appears. 4. Choose the local folder you want to keep in sync. After sign-in, the client places an icon in the Windows system tray or the macOS menu bar. Selecting the icon opens a status panel listing recent activity, a pause control, and a link to preferences.

chunks.heading: Overview and system requirements
chunks.text: A small check mark on the icon means everything is up to date, while a rotating arrow shows that files are currently being transferred. The same behavior applies on every plan: Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting and file limits
chunks.text:
Most problems in Nimbus Sync 4.x appear as a message in the status panel, together with a short error code. This section covers the situations administrators ran into most often. If the client stops syncing and shows error E4012, the license check failed. This usually happens when the machine has been offline for a long stretch, the system clock is wrong, or the account was recently moved to a different plan. To recover, restart the client so that it rechecks the license:

1. Right-click or Control-click the Nimbus Sync icon. 2. Choose Quit from the menu. 3. Reopen Nimbus Sync from your applications list. 4.

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting and file limits
chunks.text: Wait for the icon to settle on the check mark. If the message returns after the restart, confirm that you are signed in to the correct account and that the computer can reach the internet, then try again. File size is the other common source of confusion. The maximum file size in 4.x is 50 GB. Anything larger is skipped, and the file is listed in the activity view with a note that it could not be uploaded. To work around this, split large archives into smaller parts, or compress and trim the contents before placing them in the synced folder. Files that are within the limit will continue to sync normally while skipped items remain flagged in the activity list.

chunks.heading: Dashboard widgets and refresh in Analytics 1.x
chunks.text:
Nimbus Analytics 1.x is retired. It was replaced by Analytics 2.0 in January 2026, and this guide is kept only for teams that still need to understand older dashboards. Every dashboard in 1.x is built from widgets, and the number you can place on a single dashboard depends on your plan. Starter allows 8 widgets, Pro allows 25, and Enterprise allows 100. Once you reach your limit, the Add Widget button is disabled until you remove an existing widget. To add a widget:
1. Open the dashboard and choose Edit. 2. Select Add Widget in the top toolbar. 3. Pick a widget type and configure it. 4.

chunks.heading: Dashboard widgets and refresh in Analytics 1.x
chunks.text: Choose Save to place it on the canvas. Enterprise dashboards refresh every 5 minutes, so the figures shown there stay current without a manual reload. If you are planning a move to 2.0, review which widgets you rely on most before you begin.

chunks.heading: What's new and fixed in this release
chunks.text: Orbit Sync, made by Orbit Labs, gets a focused update this release that addresses a long-standing upload problem and expands what the Pro plan covers. New: The Orbit Pro plan now includes SSO. Workspace admins on Pro can open Settings, choose Security, and find the single sign-on options there. Teams that previously needed to move to a higher plan for this no longer have to. Fixed: Some customers saw E4012 'quota exceeded' errors when uploading large files, even though their workspace still had room available. The upload check now evaluates your quota correctly, so large uploads complete as expected.

chunks.heading: What's new and fixed in this release
chunks.text: If you hit this error earlier, simply retry the upload from the sync queue; no changes to your account are needed. As always, update your desktop client to receive the fix, and contact Orbit Labs support if you notice anything unusual.

chunks.heading: Passkey sign-in and pricing note
chunks.text:
Orbit Sync now offers passkey sign-in as the primary login method. When you open the sign-in screen, the first option is a Continue with passkey button, and the password field moves below it as a fallback. To set up a passkey:
1. Sign in as usual and open Account settings. 2. Select Security, then Add a passkey. 3. Approve the prompt on your device using your fingerprint, face unlock or device PIN. 4. Give the passkey a recognizable name, such as Work laptop. After that, you confirm on your device instead of typing a password. Passkeys work across the Free, Starter, Pro and Enterprise plans.

chunks.heading: Passkey sign-in and pricing note
chunks.text: A pricing reminder for teams planning upgrades: Orbit Pro is $22 per user per month. Your billing page shows the current rate for your workspace, so you can check it before adding seats. If a passkey prompt does not appear, make sure your browser is up to date and try again.

chunks.heading: Orbit Sync 5.1: Release Notes
chunks.text: Orbit Sync 5.1 is now available to all plans: Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise. This release focuses on throughput and platform coverage. Higher burst limit for Orbit Pro. The burst limit for Orbit Pro workspaces has been raised to 200 requests per second. Teams that sync large batches of changes at once should see fewer throttled calls during short spikes. No configuration is required. The new limit applies automatically to existing Pro workspaces. To confirm it, open Settings, choose Usage, and look at the rate limit panel for your workspace. Ubuntu 24.04 support. The Orbit Sync client and background service can now be installed on Ubuntu 24.04.

chunks.heading: Orbit Sync 5.1: Release Notes
chunks.text:
Install it the same way as on earlier supported releases:

1. Download the package from your account dashboard. 2. Install it with your package manager. 3. Sign in and pick the folders you want to sync. Existing installations are unaffected by this release.

chunks.heading: Rate limit errors and SLA credits
chunks.text: This release of the Orbit Sync API changes how we report throttled requests and clarifies how we compensate you when service falls short. Changed: Orbit API errors over the rate limit now return E4290 with HTTP 503. Previously, clients saw a generic error body that was hard to tell apart from other failures. If your integration retries on specific status codes, update your handling so it matches on the E4290 code in the response body. Back off before retrying, and avoid tight retry loops that keep you throttled. Policy: Orbit SLA credits are 5% for any month below 99.9%. Credits apply across Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise workspaces. You can review uptime for your workspace in the Orbit Sync dashboard under Settings, then Service Status. Contact Orbit Labs support to request a credit.

chunks.heading: Q1 2027: Identity and sign-in
chunks.text: This section covers the identity work we have planned for the first quarter of 2027. Nothing described here has been released. Timing and scope may change as we build, so please do not base production plans on these items until they appear in the release notes. SCIM provisioning for Pro. In Q1 2027 we plan to bring SCIM provisioning to the Pro plan. The goal is that an admin can connect an identity provider to a Nimbus workspace, so people are created, updated, and deactivated automatically as they join, change roles, or leave the company. Today that work is done by hand in the Members list.

chunks.heading: Q1 2027: Identity and sign-in
chunks.text: This item is planned, not released, and it is not available on Pro yet. Passkeys as a primary sign-in method. Also planned for Q1 2027, passkeys will become a primary sign-in method instead of only a second step for two-factor authentication. We expect the experience to look like this: on the sign-in screen, a person chooses to continue with a passkey, confirms with their device using a fingerprint, face unlock, or device PIN, and is signed in without typing a password. Details such as admin controls and fallback options are still being designed. Each roadmap item carries a status label of Planned, In progress, or Released. Everything on this page is currently marked Planned. If one of these items matters to your team, tell your account contact or send feedback from the Help menu in Nimbus Platform.

chunks.heading: Q2 2027: Analytics access and API capacity
chunks.text: This section lists the items we are targeting for the second quarter of 2027. As with the rest of the roadmap, these are plans only. None of them has been released, and the final shape of each may change before it ships. Nimbus Analytics on the Free plan. In Q2 2027 we plan to make Nimbus Analytics available on the Free plan, with 3 widgets per dashboard. The idea is that a small team can open Analytics, create a dashboard, and add a few widgets to see how their workspace is doing before deciding whether they need a larger plan.

chunks.heading: Q2 2027: Analytics access and API capacity
chunks.text: Teams that want to build richer dashboards would still look at the paid plans. We will publish the exact setup steps and any onboarding prompts in the release notes when the work is ready. Higher burst limit for Pro. Also planned for Q2 2027 is raising the Pro burst limit to 150 requests per second. Burst limits matter for workloads that send many calls in a short spike, such as a nightly import or a batch of webhook retries. Once the change is released, Pro customers should not need to change their integrations to benefit from it, though we still recommend handling rate-limit responses gracefully. We will move each item from Planned to In progress on this roadmap when development begins, and to Released once it is live.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Sync 6: planned changes
chunks.text: Nimbus Sync 6 is planned for mid-2027. Nothing described here has been released, and scope and timing may change as we continue development. This roadmap entry is meant to help administrators plan ahead, not to commit us to a delivery schedule. Planned for Enterprise workspaces is a maximum file size of 500 GB, intended for teams that move very large media, engineering, or archive files. Free, Starter, and Pro plans are not covered by this item, and current limits for those plans stay as they are today. We also plan to drop support for macOS 13 in Nimbus Sync 6.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Sync 6: planned changes
chunks.text: If your organization still has Macs on that operating system, we suggest reviewing your upgrade schedule now so devices can move to a supported release before the new version arrives. Current releases of the desktop client will keep working as documented until then.
