chunks.heading: E4012 investigation (DRAFT, unconfirmed)
chunks.text:
DRAFT – internal notes, not reviewed or approved. Nothing here should be shared with customers yet. Context: Pro-plan users of Nimbus Sync report that the desktop client shows E4012 when a laptop wakes from sleep. Syncing usually resumes after a manual restart of the client. Working theory (unconfirmed): E4012 after sleep is caused by the OS suspending the refresh timer. If the timer never fires while the machine is asleep, the session token may lapse before the client notices, and the next request fails. To help confirm this:
1. Reproduce on a test machine by putting it to sleep, then waking it. 2.

chunks.heading: E4012 investigation (DRAFT, unconfirmed)
chunks.text: Capture the client log from the moment of wake. 3. Compare the timer's last tick against the first failed request. Engineering estimated the fix would ship in Sync 5.4. Treat that as a rough estimate, not a commitment, until the root cause is verified. Support should keep suggesting a client restart as the interim workaround.

chunks.heading: Discounting guidelines for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text:
Discounting is a tool for closing deals that are already healthy, not a way to rescue a weak opportunity. Before you talk about price, make sure you understand the buyer's goals, who signs the contract, and how long they expect to use Nimbus Platform. Discounts work best when you trade them for something concrete, such as a longer commitment or a faster signature. For Pro, account executives may offer up to 15% off for multi-year deals with manager approval. That approval is part of the rule, not a courtesy. Here is the usual flow:

1. Confirm the customer wants a multi-year agreement and has the authority to commit. 2.

chunks.heading: Discounting guidelines for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text: Build the quote in the deal record and enter the proposed discount in the discount field. 3. Submit it for manager approval and add a short note explaining what the customer is giving in return. 4. Send the quote only after you see the approved status on the deal. Do not hint at a discount in email or chat before approval comes through. Customers remember numbers, and walking one back damages trust. Enterprise works differently because scope drives the price. Never quote Enterprise prices in writing before a scoping call.

chunks.heading: Discounting guidelines for Nimbus Platform
chunks.text: If a prospect asks for a number by email, reply that you would like to understand their requirements first and offer times to talk. After the scoping call, work with your manager on a proposal that reflects what the customer actually needs.

chunks.heading: Competitive note: Orbit Pro
chunks.text:
Prospects sometimes bring up Orbit Pro when we discuss price. Orbit Pro comes from Orbit Labs, which is a separate company with no connection to Nimbus. Be accurate about this in conversations, because buyers occasionally confuse the two vendors, especially when they have also looked at Orbit Sync. The competitive note is simple: Orbit Pro is cheaper at $22 but lacks data residency. Do not dismiss the lower price. If the buyer is a small team with no regional storage obligations, the gap may genuinely matter, and pretending otherwise will cost you credibility. Acknowledge it and move the conversation to requirements. A helpful approach:

1.

chunks.heading: Competitive note: Orbit Pro
chunks.text: Ask whether the customer has any legal, contractual, or internal rules about where their data must be stored. 2. If they do, explain that Orbit Pro does not offer data residency, so it may not meet those needs regardless of price. 3. If they do not, focus on the broader value of Nimbus Platform and on the plan that fits their stage. Avoid making claims about other Orbit Labs products or plans that you cannot verify. Stick to what the buyer can confirm on the vendor's own materials. If a deal is slipping because of price alone, bring your manager in early and review the options for the Pro discount rather than improvising a concession.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Certified Admin course
chunks.text: The Nimbus Certified Admin course is built for people who manage a Nimbus Platform workspace day to day, whether they are on the Free, Starter, Pro, or Enterprise plan. It runs as six modules, and every one is self-paced, so you can work through them during a quiet afternoon or spread them across several weeks. The course costs $199, which you pay at enrollment from the Training tab in your account. Each module combines short readings, guided walkthroughs in a sandbox workspace, and a knowledge check at the end. Once you have finished all six, you can book the certification exam.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Certified Admin course
chunks.text: It contains 60 questions, and you need a score of 70% to pass. A passing result earns you the Nimbus Certified Admin certificate, which is valid for 2 years. Before it lapses, you can renew by retaking the exam and keeping your credential current.

chunks.heading: Building with Nimbus Gateway: Developer Course
chunks.text: Building with Nimbus Gateway is a hands-on developer course for engineers who want to put the Nimbus Gateway API into production. It is organized into four modules covering authentication, rate limits, webhooks and pagination. Each module pairs a short walkthrough with a lab you complete in your own workspace, so you finish with working code rather than slide notes. Start with authentication, where you create credentials and make your first signed request. Next, the rate limits module shows how to read response headers and back off gracefully when a client is throttled. The webhooks module walks through registering an endpoint, verifying payloads and handling retries.

chunks.heading: Building with Nimbus Gateway: Developer Course
chunks.text: The final module, pagination, covers iterating through large result sets reliably. The course is free for Pro and Enterprise customers and costs $99 for everyone else. To enroll, open the Training tab in the Nimbus Platform console, select the course card, and choose Start course. Your progress is saved between sessions.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Analytics for analysts: course format
chunks.text: Nimbus Analytics for analysts is a instructor-led course for people who build and maintain reports in Nimbus Analytics every day. It is delivered as three live sessions of 90 minutes each, and the sessions are included with Enterprise. Teams on Starter or Pro can still use the product itself, but the live course is part of the Enterprise plan. Each session is hands-on. Participants work in their own workspace, so before the first session, open Nimbus Analytics and confirm you can sign in and see at least one connected data source.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Analytics for analysts: course format
chunks.text: During class, the instructor walks through a task, such as creating a new report from a source, and then you repeat it on your own data. Questions are taken in the chat panel, and the instructor answers them as the group works through each exercise. Come prepared with a real reporting question you want to answer, since examples drawn from your own work make the exercises far more useful.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: Nimbus Gateway outage on November 12, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary and impact
chunks.text: On November 12, 2026, Nimbus Gateway in the US region returned E5003 for 47 minutes. During that window, API calls routed through the affected region failed instead of reaching customer upstream services. Customers on the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans saw failed requests in their Gateway dashboards, where the error rate chart showed a sharp rise in E5003 responses. Traffic in other regions was not affected. The cause was a configuration push that removed capacity from the request routers. With too few routers left to absorb incoming traffic, the remaining routers rejected requests they could not handle.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: Nimbus Gateway outage on November 12, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary and impact
chunks.text: Our engineers identified the faulty change, reverted it, and watched the routers return to normal load before declaring the incident resolved. To prevent a repeat, we are adding capacity checks that block pushes which would reduce router capacity below a safe level. Affected customers may be eligible for service credits under their agreement. Please contact your account team or Nimbus Support to review your usage.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: Nimbus Sync delays on August 3, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary and cause
chunks.text: On August 3, 2026, customers using Nimbus Sync in the EU region saw file changes take up to 2 hours to sync across their devices. The delay affected workspaces on every plan: Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise. Files were never lost, and nothing was overwritten. Changes were saved locally and uploaded once the backlog cleared. The cause was a queue backlog that built up after a database failover. When the primary database switched to its standby, sync jobs kept arriving faster than the workers could process them, so pending changes waited in line.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: Nimbus Sync delays on August 3, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary and cause
chunks.text:
In the Nimbus Sync desktop app, affected users saw the status icon stay on "Syncing" instead of changing to "Up to date."

Our engineers drained the queue and confirmed that normal sync speed returned. No action is needed on your side. If a file still looks out of date, pause and resume sync from the app menu, then contact Support.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: Analytics dashboard refresh failures on October 2, 2026
chunks.heading: Incident summary and resolution
chunks.text: On October 2, 2026, Nimbus Analytics dashboards stopped refreshing for 3 hours. Customers on the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans saw stale data on scheduled and manual refreshes. Existing dashboards remained viewable, but charts showed the last successful values, and the refresh button in the dashboard toolbar returned a failure notice. The cause was an expired certificate on the Snowflake connector. Once it lapsed, the connector could no longer establish a trusted session with customer warehouses, so every refresh job failed at the connection step. Our on-call engineers traced the failures to the connector logs, replaced the certificate, and restarted the affected refresh workers.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: Analytics dashboard refresh failures on October 2, 2026
chunks.heading: Incident summary and resolution
chunks.text: Queued refreshes then ran in order, and dashboards returned to normal. Follow-up actions: we are adding expiry monitoring with earlier alerts for all connector certificates, and we are documenting a renewal procedure so rotation no longer depends on a single owner. Customers who still see stale data should select Refresh on the dashboard and contact support if the problem persists.

chunks.heading: Say hello to passkeys
chunks.text: Today we're introducing passkeys to Nimbus Platform, and they're available on every plan, from Free to Enterprise. For now, a passkey works as a second factor: you still enter your password, then confirm it's really you with your fingerprint, face scan, or device PIN instead of typing a code from an authenticator app. Why bother? Passkeys are tied to your device and to the Nimbus site itself, so a convincing fake login page can't trick you into handing anything over. There's also no six-digit code to read out, copy, or lose when you switch phones.

chunks.heading: Say hello to passkeys
chunks.text: To try one, open your account security settings, choose to add a second factor, and select passkey. Your browser or device will walk you through the rest in a minute or so of prompts. What about going fully passwordless? That's something we are exploring for the future, and we'll share more once we have something to show. Until then, we hope passkeys make signing in a little safer and a lot smoother.

chunks.heading: Simpler pricing, more for Pro
chunks.text: We spend a lot of time listening to how teams use Nimbus Platform, and one theme keeps coming up: pricing should be easy to understand, and the features you rely on should not hide behind a custom quote. Today we're announcing changes that move us in that direction. From September 15, 2026, SSO is part of Pro, and the Pro price becomes $24. If your team has been waiting to roll out single sign-on across your workspace, you'll no longer need to talk to sales or step up to Enterprise to get it. Admins can find the option in workspace settings once the change goes live.

chunks.heading: Simpler pricing, more for Pro
chunks.text: We're also improving things for smaller teams: Starter gets twice the storage. There's nothing to configure and no action required, since the larger allowance simply appears in your account. If you have questions about how this affects your plan, our support team is happy to walk through it with you.

chunks.heading: More room on every Pro dashboard
chunks.text:
Dashboards in Nimbus Analytics just got roomier. Pro dashboards can now hold 40 widgets, so the story you tell with your data no longer has to be split across a pile of separate boards. Why does this matter? Many teams told us they were running into the ceiling as soon as they tried to combine operational metrics, customer trends and revenue views in one place. A product lead can now keep adoption charts, support volume and release health side by side, and an executive can open a single board instead of hopping between several. To make the most of the extra space, try this:

1.

chunks.heading: More room on every Pro dashboard
chunks.text: Open an existing dashboard that feels crowded or has been split up. 2. Bring in the widgets you previously parked on other boards. 3. Group related widgets together so the page still reads from top to bottom. A bigger canvas works best with a little structure, so keep your most important numbers near the top. The change is available to Pro workspaces in Nimbus Analytics now.

chunks.heading: Nimbus comes to Tokyo
chunks.text: Today we're excited to announce that Nimbus Platform has a new home in Asia. Enterprise customers can now keep their data in the APAC (Tokyo) region, giving teams across the area a way to store and process their workloads closer to the people who rely on them. We've heard from many of you that where data lives matters. Some teams want it near their users. Others have internal policies or customer commitments that call for regional residency. Tokyo gives those teams a clear option without changing how they work day to day. Getting started is straightforward.

chunks.heading: Nimbus comes to Tokyo
chunks.text: Open your workspace settings, choose the data region section, and select APAC (Tokyo) when you set up a new workspace. If you'd like help planning the move for an existing workspace, your account team is happy to walk through it with you. Thank you to everyone who shared feedback along the way. We can't wait to see what you build in Tokyo.

chunks.heading: Fix: duplicate conflicted copies after simultaneous renames
chunks.text: This maintenance release resolves a sync issue that affected shared folders across all Nimbus Sync plans: Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise. Previously, when two devices renamed the same file while both were offline or before either change had synced, Nimbus Sync could not reconcile the two names and created duplicate conflicted copies of the file. Users would then find extra items with "conflicted copy" in the name and had to delete them by hand. This has been fixed. Nimbus Sync now recognizes that both devices changed only the file's name, picks one name, and keeps a single file. No action is needed to receive the fix once the client updates. If you still see conflicted copies created by earlier renames, review them in the folder's Activity view and remove any you no longer need. Contact Nimbus Support if you see the behavior again.

chunks.heading: Improvements: lower memory use during initial scans
chunks.text: This maintenance release of Nimbus Sync focuses on stability when you first connect a very large folder. Previously, the initial scan, which catalogs every file and subfolder before syncing begins, could take up a lot of memory on the device. This was most noticeable on older laptops and on shared machines running other applications. Nimbus Sync now uses noticeably less memory during that first pass over large folders, so the scan is less likely to slow down your computer or compete with other apps. You don't need to change any settings. To benefit, update the desktop app, then add a folder as usual.

chunks.heading: Improvements: lower memory use during initial scans
chunks.text: The status icon in the menu bar or system tray shows Scanning while the work is in progress and switches to Up to date when it finishes. The improvement applies to the Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans.

chunks.heading: Retry-After now sent when the daily quota is exhausted
chunks.text: This release makes a small but useful change to how Nimbus Gateway responds to clients that have run out of capacity. The Retry-After header is now also sent when the daily quota is exhausted. Previously, API clients that hit their daily quota received a rejection without any guidance on when to try again, so many integrations fell back to guessing or retrying aggressively. With the header present, well-behaved clients and standard HTTP libraries can pause until the quota resets instead of polling the Gateway repeatedly. No configuration is required. The behavior applies automatically to all Gateway routes on Starter, Pro, and Enterprise.

chunks.heading: Retry-After now sent when the daily quota is exhausted
chunks.text: If your client already honors Retry-After for other throttling responses, it will pick up the new behavior without code changes. If you maintain custom retry logic, review it to confirm that it reads the header on quota rejections as well.

chunks.heading: Fixed: time zone handling in scheduled reports
chunks.text:
This release fixes how Nimbus Analytics handles time zones in scheduled reports. Previously, a report could be delivered at a different local time than the one you chose, especially when the workspace time zone and your personal profile time zone did not match. Reports now run and deliver according to the time zone selected on the schedule itself. To check your existing schedules:

1. Open Reports and select the Scheduled tab. 2. Choose a report and click Edit schedule. 3. Confirm the value in the Time zone field is the one you intend. 4. Save the schedule.

chunks.heading: Fixed: time zone handling in scheduled reports
chunks.text: For example, if a team in one region schedules a weekly summary but a colleague in another region edits the recipient list, the delivery time no longer shifts. The date range inside the report also follows the schedule's time zone, so figures at the edge of a day or week group the way you expect. This fix applies to scheduled reports on the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans. No action is needed unless you previously adjusted a schedule to work around the problem. In that case, review it and reset the time zone.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Platform June 2026 release
chunks.text: This June release for Nimbus Platform, available on the Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans, focuses on finding your content faster and keeping shared files under tighter control. Search now finds text inside slides. When you type a phrase into the search bar at the top of the workspace, results include presentations whose slide content matches, not only titles and descriptions. Matching slides appear with a short preview so you can tell at a glance whether you have the right deck. For example, searching for a product name mentioned on a single slide in a quarterly review will now bring that presentation to the top of your results.

chunks.heading: Nimbus Platform June 2026 release
chunks.text: Admins can disable public links for the whole workspace. To use it, open Admin Settings, choose Sharing, and switch off the Public links option. Once it is off, members can no longer create new public links, and sharing continues to work for people who are signed in to your workspace. Review your sharing policy with your team before changing it.

chunks.heading: Shared drives: larger teams, same simple setup
chunks.text: With the July 2026 release of Nimbus Platform, shared drives can now have up to 600 members. This gives larger departments, cross-functional programs, and project groups room to work from a single drive instead of splitting content across several smaller ones. The update is available on the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans. To add people, open the shared drive, select Members from the drive header, and choose Add members. You can search by name or email address, then assign a role to each person before confirming. Existing drives pick up the new capacity automatically, so no migration or settings change is needed.

chunks.heading: Shared drives: larger teams, same simple setup
chunks.text: For example, a company-wide onboarding drive can now include every new hire along with the HR staff and managers who support them. Drive owners can still review and update roles at any time from the same Members panel, which keeps access easy to manage as your team grows.

chunks.heading: SSO now available on Pro
chunks.text:
Single sign-on is now available on the Pro plan, following the September 15, 2026 pricing update. Previously, SSO was offered only to Enterprise workspaces. Pro administrators can now connect their identity provider and let teammates sign in with existing company credentials. To get started:
1. Open Nimbus Platform and go to Settings, then Security. 2. Select the Single sign-on tab and choose your identity provider from the list. 3. Paste in the metadata details from your provider and save the configuration. 4. Use the Test connection button to confirm a sign-in works before you enable it for everyone.

chunks.heading: SSO now available on Pro
chunks.text: For example, an admin at a growing team might connect their provider on Monday, test with their own account, and then switch SSO on for the whole workspace. Enterprise customers keep their existing SSO setup, and nothing changes for them. Workspaces on other plans will see an upgrade prompt on the Security tab.

chunks.doc_title: How long does SSO setup take?
chunks.heading: How long SSO setup takes
chunks.text:
Most admins finish SSO setup in under an hour. SSO is available in Nimbus Platform on the Pro and Enterprise plans. The time you need depends mostly on how quickly you can get the right details from your identity provider. Before you start, have the following ready:

1. Admin access to both Nimbus Platform and your identity provider. 2. The metadata or sign-in details your identity provider supplies. 3. A list of the people who will sign in through SSO. Once you've entered the connection details and saved them, test the setup with a second admin account before enforcing SSO. This matters because enforcing SSO changes how everyone signs in.

chunks.doc_title: How long does SSO setup take?
chunks.heading: How long SSO setup takes
chunks.text: If something is misconfigured, you could be locked out. A second admin who signs in successfully through your identity provider confirms the connection works. After that test passes, you can safely turn on enforcement for the rest of your workspace.

chunks.heading: Exporting all workspace data
chunks.text: If you need a complete copy of your workspace, whether for backup, compliance review, or a move to another tool, Nimbus Platform lets you export everything in one step. Only workspace Owners can start an export, and this applies on every plan, from Free through Enterprise. To begin, sign in and open Settings, then choose Export from the menu. Select the option to export all workspace data and confirm your request. Nimbus gathers every file along with its metadata and packages it into a single ZIP archive. Larger workspaces may take a while to prepare, so you can leave the page and come back.

chunks.heading: Exporting all workspace data
chunks.text: When the archive is ready, you will see a download link in the Export section. Exports stay downloadable for 7 days, so save the file somewhere safe before then. If the link expires, an Owner can simply start a new export from the same screen. If the Export option does not appear, check that your role is Owner.

chunks.doc_title: Can I invite guests on the Free plan?
chunks.heading: Guest access on the Free plan
chunks.text:
Guests cannot be invited on the Free plan. If you try to add someone from outside your workspace, you will see the Invite guest option appear unavailable, along with a short note explaining that your current plan does not include it. Guest access needs Starter or higher, so you would need to upgrade before external collaborators can join. If you only need to bring in teammates, you can still add them as regular members from Settings > People. To explore guest access, follow these steps:

1. Open Settings and select Billing. 2. Review the plans listed under Change plan. 3. Choose Starter or a higher plan and confirm the change.

chunks.doc_title: Can I invite guests on the Free plan?
chunks.heading: Guest access on the Free plan
chunks.text: Once your workspace is on a qualifying plan, the Invite guest option becomes available on the People screen. Only workspace owners and billing admins can change plans, so ask one of them if you don't see the Billing tab.

chunks.heading: My API key stopped working
chunks.text: If requests to Nimbus Gateway suddenly fail even though nothing changed in your code, the most likely cause is an expired key. API keys expire after 1 year, and any call made with an expired key returns E4011. You can confirm this by checking the response body in your logs or in your HTTP client. This applies to the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans. To get back up and running, create a new key. Open Settings > Developer > API keys, select Create key, give it a recognizable name, and copy the value when it appears.

chunks.heading: My API key stopped working
chunks.text: Then replace the old key in your application, environment variables, or secrets manager and redeploy if needed. Once your traffic succeeds with the new key, you can remove the expired one from the same list so it doesn't cause confusion later. If you still see errors after swapping keys, double-check that no other services are still using the old value.

chunks.doc_title: Which currencies can I pay in?
chunks.heading: Which currencies can I pay in?
chunks.text: Nimbus bills in US dollars, euros and Japanese yen. These currencies apply to Nimbus Platform subscriptions on the Starter, Pro and Enterprise plans. The Free plan has no charges, so no billing currency is needed. You choose a currency when you first add a payment method, and your invoices are issued in that currency from then on. To check which one your account uses, open Billing from the main menu, then select the Invoices tab. The currency appears next to each invoice total. If you need to change currencies, contact our support team through the Help menu and let us know which of the three you would like to use.

chunks.doc_title: Which currencies can I pay in?
chunks.heading: Which currencies can I pay in?
chunks.text: An account owner or billing admin must make the request. Your card issuer or bank may also apply its own conversion if your card is held in a different currency, so it is worth checking with them about any extra fees on their side.

chunks.doc_title: How many devices can I use with Nimbus Sync?
chunks.heading: How many devices can I use with Nimbus Sync?
chunks.text: The number of devices you can connect to Nimbus Sync depends on your plan. Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise each come with their own device limit, and you can find the exact figure for each plan on the pricing sheet. We don't list the numbers here so that you always see the current ones in one place. If you try to add a device after reaching your limit, Nimbus Sync stops the sign-in and shows error E4019. Your existing devices keep syncing as usual, and no files are affected. To fix it, open Settings, choose Devices, and review the list of connected devices.

chunks.doc_title: How many devices can I use with Nimbus Sync?
chunks.heading: How many devices can I use with Nimbus Sync?
chunks.text: Select the three-dot menu beside any device you no longer use and choose Remove. Then try adding the new device again. If you need more room, go to Billing and compare plans to see whether an upgrade fits your needs. Account owners and admins can change plans and remove devices.

chunks.doc_title: How do I request an SLA credit?
chunks.heading: Requesting an SLA credit for Nimbus Gateway
chunks.text: If Nimbus Gateway did not meet the uptime commitment included with your Pro or Enterprise plan, you can ask for a service credit. Requests are handled through Support, so there is no button in the billing settings for this. To get started, sign in and open a support ticket from the Help menu. In the ticket, include the affected month and your workspace ID. You can find the workspace ID under Settings, on the workspace overview screen. If you manage more than one workspace, submit the details for each one so the team can review the right usage.

chunks.doc_title: How do I request an SLA credit?
chunks.heading: Requesting an SLA credit for Nimbus Gateway
chunks.text: It also helps to describe what you noticed, such as failed requests or timeouts, along with approximate times. Our team will review the request against our service records and reply in the ticket. If the credit is approved, it is applied to your next invoice. You do not need to take any further action, and the adjustment will appear as a separate line item on that invoice.

chunks.heading: Is there a mobile app?
chunks.text: Yes. Nimbus Platform has mobile apps so you can stay connected to your workspace when you're away from your desk. The apps are available for iOS 17 or later and Android 13 or later, so check your device's operating system before you install. To find your version on iPhone, open Settings, tap General, then tap About. On Android, open Settings and look under About phone. To get started, search for Nimbus in the App Store or Google Play, install the app, and sign in with the same email and password you use on the web. If your organization uses single sign-on, choose that option on the sign-in screen instead.

chunks.heading: Is there a mobile app?
chunks.text: The mobile apps are available on every plan, including Free, Starter, Pro, and Enterprise. If you can't sign in, confirm that your account is active and that you're using the correct workspace address. Your account administrator can help if you're still stuck.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: sign-in failures on June 18, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary, cause, and follow-up
chunks.text: On June 18, 2026, users in Nimbus Platform workspaces that sign in through Okta could not complete SSO for 25 minutes. People who clicked the Okta tile or chose "Continue with SSO" on the Nimbus sign-in page saw a generic authentication error and were returned to the login screen. Workspaces using email and password, or other identity providers, were not affected, and sessions that were already active continued to work. The cause was an expired signing certificate used to validate SAML assertions for the Okta integration. Our renewal reminder had been routed to a mailbox that nobody monitored, so the expiry went unnoticed until sign-in requests began failing.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: sign-in failures on June 18, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary, cause, and follow-up
chunks.text: Engineers installed a renewed certificate, and sign-ins recovered. We are moving certificate alerts to the on-call rotation, adding an automated expiry check, and reviewing every other integration certificate for the same gap. Admins do not need to take any action.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: webhook delays on September 21, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary and impact
chunks.text: On September 21, 2026, webhook deliveries from Nimbus Gateway were delayed by up to 40 minutes. Customers on the Starter, Pro, and Enterprise plans may have seen outbound webhooks arrive well after the triggering event. No events were lost. Every webhook that Gateway accepted was queued, retried as needed, and eventually delivered to its configured endpoint. What you may have noticed: in the Gateway dashboard, the Webhooks view showed deliveries with a status of Pending for longer than usual, and receiving systems saw events arrive later than their timestamps suggested.

chunks.doc_title: Incident report: webhook delays on September 21, 2026
chunks.heading: Summary and impact
chunks.text: Event payloads and ordering metadata were unchanged, so you can rely on the event timestamp rather than arrival time when reconciling data. Follow-up: our team is reviewing queue monitoring and alerting so that a growing delivery backlog is caught and addressed sooner. If your integration still looks out of sync, contact Nimbus Support.

chunks.heading: Sync 5.2: smoother sign-in after sleep
chunks.text: If you use Nimbus Sync on a Pro plan, you may know the moment: you open your laptop lid, expect your files to catch up, and instead see an E4012 sign-in error. Sync 5.2 ends those errors for the many Pro users who ran into them after waking their machines. The fix works quietly in the background. When your laptop comes out of sleep, Sync now checks your session before it tries to reconnect, so you no longer get kicked back to the sign-in screen. Your menu bar icon simply shows the usual syncing status and picks up where it left off.

chunks.heading: Sync 5.2: smoother sign-in after sleep
chunks.text: To get the update, open the Sync menu, choose Check for updates, and restart when prompted. If you manage a team, let your colleagues know. Close the lid, open it later, and get back to work.

chunks.doc_title: Legal holds for whole shared drives
chunks.heading: Legal holds for whole shared drives
chunks.text: Anyone who has supported an eDiscovery request knows the pain of preserving files one folder at a time. Enterprise legal teams can now hold an entire shared drive in one step, and we think it will change how matters get started in Nimbus Platform. Here's how it looks in practice. Open the shared drive from the admin console, choose Legal hold from the drive's action menu, and pick the matter it belongs to. Confirm, and Nimbus applies the hold to everything in the drive, including files added afterward. Custodians keep working as usual, but deletion and permanent purge are blocked for held content.

chunks.doc_title: Legal holds for whole shared drives
chunks.heading: Legal holds for whole shared drives
chunks.text: Imagine a contract dispute involving your procurement team. Instead of building a list of folders and hoping nothing was missed, counsel selects the procurement drive and moves on. When the matter closes, releasing the hold is just as direct, and the activity is recorded in the audit log for your records. This capability is available on the Enterprise plan.

chunks.doc_title: Nimbus vs. Orbit: what to compare
chunks.heading: Nimbus vs. Orbit: what to compare
chunks.text: If you're weighing Nimbus Platform against Orbit Sync, start by remembering they come from different companies and solve problems in different ways. Orbit Sync is made by Orbit Labs, so a fair evaluation means looking at what each tool does in your own environment rather than matching feature names line by line. A useful approach is to write down your real workflow first. Who needs access? Where must your data live? How much time will your team spend on setup and upkeep? On the residency question, Nimbus offers data residency in three regions, so check whether those regions line up with your compliance needs. Then turn to budget.

chunks.doc_title: Nimbus vs. Orbit: what to compare
chunks.heading: Nimbus vs. Orbit: what to compare
chunks.text: We encourage buyers to compare total cost, not list price. Consider onboarding effort, admin time, and what happens when your team grows and you move between Free, Starter, Pro, or Enterprise. A cheaper sticker price can hide expensive surprises, and a trial with your own data will show you far more than any brochure.

chunks.heading: Deploying Nimbus Sync at scale: course overview
chunks.text: Deploying Nimbus Sync at scale is a short training course for administrators who roll out Nimbus Sync across many workstations. It is organized into two modules. The first module covers silent installs, showing how to prepare an installer package, pass configuration options so no prompts appear for the end user, and confirm that each machine registers correctly with your workspace. The second module covers device management, where you learn to review enrolled devices in the admin console, group them, and remove devices that are lost or retired. Each module combines a walkthrough with a guided exercise in a sandbox workspace.

chunks.heading: Deploying Nimbus Sync at scale: course overview
chunks.text: The course is designed for teams on the Pro and Enterprise plans, and it is free for Enterprise customers. Before you begin, make sure you have admin access to your Nimbus Sync workspace and a test machine where you can safely try an installation.

chunks.heading: Nimbus security for admins: course overview
chunks.text: Nimbus security for admins is a single module for Nimbus Platform administrators on the Pro and Enterprise plans. It covers three areas that most security reviews ask about: single sign-on, two-factor authentication and audit logs. The module takes about 45 minutes, so it fits comfortably into a lunch break or a quiet part of an onboarding week. You begin in the Admin console, where you open the Security area and review how members currently sign in. From there the module walks through connecting an identity provider for SSO, then requiring a second verification step for your workspace.

chunks.heading: Nimbus security for admins: course overview
chunks.text: Finally, you open the audit log viewer, filter events by person or action, and practice tracing a changed setting back to the administrator who made it. Each section ends with a short exercise in a sandbox workspace, so you can try settings without affecting real users. Completing the module is a good first step before rolling out stricter sign-in rules to your whole organization.

chunks.heading: Proposal: raise Pro burst limit (draft)
chunks.text:
**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not scheduled, and not to be shared with customers.**

This page collects early thinking on raising the Nimbus Gateway burst limit for the Pro plan. The proposal is to raise the Pro burst limit to 150 requests per second in 2027. Nothing here is confirmed, and the timing could change or the proposal could be dropped entirely.

**Context**
Support has seen Pro customers hit throttling during short traffic spikes, even when their sustained usage is well within plan. A higher burst ceiling would help with those spikes without changing how sustained usage is handled.

**Open questions**
1. What infrastructure headroom do we need before committing? 2.

chunks.heading: Proposal: raise Pro burst limit (draft)
chunks.text: How should Pro sit relative to Enterprise? 3. Does the Gateway dashboard need new wording for throttling messages? Please add comments below rather than editing the proposal. Product and Engineering will review before any decision is made.

chunks.heading: Handling objections about SLA credits
chunks.text: Prospects on Starter, Pro, and Enterprise evaluations sometimes ask what happens if Nimbus Platform misses its uptime commitment. This usually comes up late in procurement, often from a security or legal reviewer rather than the day-to-day buyer. Keep your answer calm and factual. Acknowledge that reliability matters, then explain that service commitments and remedies are documented in one place. If a prospect asks about SLA credits, point them to the published SLA; do not promise custom credits. Reps should never improvise terms, even when a deal is close to signing or the buyer says a competitor offered something richer.

chunks.heading: Handling objections about SLA credits
chunks.text: Side commitments made in email or on calls create confusion later and are not honored by support or finance. A good response sounds like this: "Our SLA is public, and it spells out how credits work. I'm happy to send the link and walk through it with you." If the buyer pushes for different terms, note the request and bring in your manager rather than answering yourself.

chunks.heading: Quota behavior in Gateway 2.x (retired)
chunks.text:
This section describes how request limits worked in Nimbus Gateway 2.x, which is now retired. Unlike newer approaches to traffic control, Gateway 2.x had no burst limit, only a daily quota. Clients could send requests as fast as they liked until the day's allowance was used up, so sudden spikes were never throttled on their own. When the allowance ran out, the gateway rejected further calls. Quota errors returned HTTP 403 with E4030, rather than a dedicated rate-limit status. To investigate a rejection in the legacy console:
1. Open the Usage tab for your gateway. 2. Check the daily quota meter at the top of the page. 3.

chunks.heading: Quota behavior in Gateway 2.x (retired)
chunks.text: Search the request log for responses carrying E4030. 4. Confirm the timestamps fall after the meter reached its end. If your plan is Starter, Pro, or Enterprise, quota was applied per day, so access resumed once the next daily period began.

chunks.heading: Sync shows E4012 every morning
chunks.text:
Subject: Sync shows E4012 every morning

Customer: Hi team, we're on the Pro plan and sign in to Nimbus Sync through Okta SSO. Every morning when I open my laptop lid, Sync shows E4012 and stops syncing. If I sign out and back in through Okta, it works again for the rest of the day. It happens on my whole team's machines, so it seems tied to the laptop waking from sleep. Is there a setting we're missing? Agent reply: Thanks for the detailed description. This looks like the session token expiring while the laptop sleeps, and Sync doesn't re-authenticate with Okta when it wakes.

chunks.heading: Sync shows E4012 every morning
chunks.text: Please install Sync 5.1, which retries automatically after wake, so you shouldn't need to sign out and back in. A full fix is coming, and we'll update this ticket when it ships. Until you've upgraded, signing in again through Okta is the best workaround. Let us know if the error continues after updating.

chunks.doc_title: What SLA credit do we get for the Gateway outage?
chunks.heading: Ticket: SLA credit for the Gateway outage
chunks.text:
Customer message:
Hi team, our Enterprise Nimbus Gateway deployment was down during the outage on November 12, 2026, and several of our API clients failed for the duration. Could you tell us what SLA credit we are entitled to for that incident? We need to report it to our finance and procurement groups, so a clear answer in writing would help. Please also tell us whether we need to submit a formal claim form or whether you can apply the credit directly to our account. Agent reply:
Hello, and thanks for reaching out. I'm sorry about the disruption on November 12, 2026.

chunks.doc_title: What SLA credit do we get for the Gateway outage?
chunks.heading: Ticket: SLA credit for the Gateway outage
chunks.text: For incidents like this we usually give a 5% credit, but I can't confirm that figure for your account yet. I've escalated your request to your account team, who can review the contract terms and the outage impact. They will follow up with you directly on the claim process and the final amount. In the meantime, please keep any logs or timestamps showing failed requests, since they may speed up the review. I'll update this ticket as soon as I hear back.

chunks.heading: 429 responses during nightly import
chunks.text:
Customer message:
Hi team, our nightly import job through Nimbus Gateway has started failing partway through. Most requests go through fine, but then we begin receiving HTTP 429 responses with the code E4290 in the response body. The job runs from a scheduled worker that loops over our exported records and sends them to the Gateway endpoint as quickly as it can. We are on the Pro plan and haven't changed the script recently. Nothing looks wrong in the dashboard, so we're not sure what is triggering this. Can you tell us what is happening and how to get the import finishing again? Agent reply:
Hello, thanks for the details.

chunks.heading: 429 responses during nightly import
chunks.text: The E4290 error means your client is being rate limited by Gateway. The Pro burst limit is 50 requests per second, and your import loop is exceeding it when it sends records in a tight cycle. Please slow down the import by adding a short pause between requests or by lowering the number of parallel workers. If a 429 still comes back, wait briefly before retrying that request. Let us know how the next run goes.

chunks.heading: Invoice shows $8 per Starter seat
chunks.text:
Customer message:
Hi team, I'm on the Starter plan for Nimbus Platform and I just opened the latest invoice in Billing. The line item says $8 per seat, but that doesn't match what I expected to be charged based on the pricing page. Can you explain why the invoice shows $8 per seat? I'd like to understand it before I forward the invoice to our finance contact. Thanks. Agent reply:
Hi, thanks for writing in and for checking the invoice carefully. The invoice you opened covers a 2025 renewal, and it was issued at the old price, which is why the per-seat amount looks different from what you see now.

chunks.heading: Invoice shows $8 per Starter seat
chunks.text: Nothing is wrong with your account, and the line item reflects the rate that applied when that renewal was billed. If you open Billing and go to Invoices, each invoice lists the period it covers, so you can confirm which one you're viewing. Let us know if you have other questions.

chunks.doc_title: Can we use OneLogin for SSO?
chunks.heading: Can we use OneLogin for SSO?
chunks.text:
Customer message (Nimbus Platform, Pro plan): Hi team, I'm the admin for our workspace and we're getting ready to roll out single sign-on. Our company uses OneLogin as its identity provider. I looked through the SSO section of the admin settings and the documentation, but I couldn't tell whether OneLogin is supported. Can we use it with our Pro plan? I'd like to confirm before I ask our IT group to set up the connector on their side. Thanks, Dana

Agent reply: Hi Dana, thanks for reaching out.

chunks.doc_title: Can we use OneLogin for SSO?
chunks.heading: Can we use OneLogin for SSO?
chunks.text: OneLogin isn't on our documented list of identity providers, but it should probably work, since it supports SAML and that's the standard our SSO setup relies on. I'd suggest creating a custom SAML app in OneLogin and entering the details in the SSO page under admin settings. Test with one account first before enforcing it for everyone. If you hit problems, send us a screenshot of the error and we'll take a look.

chunks.heading: Ticket: Is SSO available on Starter?
chunks.text:
Customer (Dana R., Nimbus Platform, Starter plan):
Hi team, we're a small company evaluating Nimbus Platform and our IT lead wants everyone to sign in through our identity provider. We're on the Starter plan right now. Is SSO available for us, or would we have to move up to a higher plan first? We'd like to know before we invite the rest of the staff. Support agent reply (Marcus T.):
Hi Dana, thanks for reaching out. Yes, Starter can buy SSO as a $3 add-on, so you don't need to change plans. An account owner can add it from the billing area of your workspace settings.

chunks.heading: Ticket: Is SSO available on Starter?
chunks.text: Once it's on your account, an admin can open the security section and begin connecting your identity provider. I'd suggest finishing the setup before inviting everyone, so people sign in the right way from day one. Let us know if you get stuck during configuration and we'll walk through it with you. Status: Answered. Awaiting customer confirmation.

chunks.heading: Pro price after renewal
chunks.text:
Subject: Pro price after renewal
Product: Nimbus Platform (Pro plan)

Customer:
Hi, our workspace is on the Pro plan and we signed up at $20. Our renewal is coming up and I want to be sure there are no surprises on the invoice. Can you tell me what happens to our price when the plan renews? I looked under Settings, then Billing, and only saw the current amount, not anything about the next cycle. We'd like to budget properly before finance reviews it, so a clear answer would help a lot. Thanks! Support agent:

chunks.heading: Pro price after renewal

The new amount will show on your next invoice, and you can review invoices anytime from the Billing page in your workspace settings. Let us know if you have any other questions about your subscription and we'll be glad to help. Status: Replied, awaiting customer

chunks.doc_title: Legal hold on a shared drive
chunks.heading: Legal hold on a shared drive

They want everything in the drive preserved exactly as it is, including anything people add or change from here on. Can you tell us how to do this, or whether it needs to go through you? chunks.doc_title: Legal hold on a shared drive
chunks.heading: Legal hold on a shared drive
chunks.text: Agent reply: Hello, thanks for the clear details. This is done. chunks.doc_title: Free workspace locked after pricing change
chunks.heading: Free workspace locked after pricing change
chunks.text:
Subject: Free workspace locked after pricing change

Customer: Hi, our team has used Nimbus Platform on the Free plan for a long time. Today my newest teammate, the fourth person I added to the workspace, can sign in but can't edit anything. Every page shows as read-only, and she gets a banner when she tries to change a document. Nothing changed on our side. Did something happen with pricing? We're a small nonprofit and need everyone working again as soon as possible. Agent reply: Thanks for writing in, and sorry for the disruption. Free now allows 3 users, so the fourth user is being blocked from editing.

chunks.doc_title: Free workspace locked after pricing change
chunks.heading: Free workspace locked after pricing change
chunks.text: You have two options: upgrade the workspace to a paid plan, or remove a user. To remove someone, open Settings, choose Members, and select Remove next to the person's name. Once your workspace is back within the Free limit, editing should work again for the remaining members. Let us know if the banner persists afterward.

chunks.heading: Dashboard refresh too slow
chunks.text:
Subject: Dashboard refresh too slow

Customer message:
Hi team, we are on the Pro plan and use Nimbus Analytics to monitor our daily sales numbers. I noticed that our dashboards refresh only every 15 minutes. When we publish a new campaign, the tiles on the main overview board stay stale for a long time, and my colleagues keep reloading the browser tab hoping for fresh data. The refresh timestamp in the top right corner confirms the gap. Is something misconfigured on our workspace, or is this a fault? We would like the boards to feel closer to live. Agent reply:
Hello, and thanks for reaching out.

chunks.heading: Dashboard refresh too slow
chunks.text: I checked your workspace and nothing is misconfigured. A refresh interval of 15 minutes is expected on Pro, so what you are seeing is normal behavior and not a fault. Reloading the browser tab will not speed it up, because the data is refreshed on the schedule rather than by the page. If you would like to talk through your reporting needs, reply here and I can point you to the right person on our team. Best regards, Nimbus Support

chunks.heading: Widget limit on Pro

chunks.heading: Cannot add a sixth device on Starter
chunks.text:
Customer message:
Hi, I just got a new work laptop and installed Nimbus Sync on it. When I sign in and try to link it to my account, it fails with an error and the laptop never shows up in my device list. This is the sixth device I'm trying to add. I'm on the Starter plan, and my phone, tablet and desktop machines are all syncing fine. I don't want to lose any files while I sort this out. Hello, thanks for writing in.

chunks.heading: Cannot add a sixth device on Starter
chunks.text: Your account has reached the number of devices it can link, so the sixth device can't be added. To fix it, open Nimbus Sync on a device that's already connected, go to Settings > Devices, and remove an old device you no longer use. Then sign in again on the new laptop and it should register. Your files stay in your account, so removing a device won't delete them. Let us know how it goes.

chunks.heading: Max upload size
chunks.text:
Subject: Max upload size
Product: Nimbus Sync | Plan: Starter

Customer:
Hi team, we're on the Starter plan and have started using Nimbus Sync for our video production folders. Some of our project exports are very large, and before I set up the sync for the whole team I'd like to know what to expect. What is the largest single file we can sync? I don't want the client to hit a wall halfway through a transfer and have to start again. If the answer depends on our plan, please tell me what applies to Starter specifically. Thanks for your help.

chunks.heading: Max upload size
chunks.text:
Support agent:

chunks.heading: SMS 2FA going away
chunks.text:
**Posted by dana_ops:**
I just saw the banner in Nimbus Platform saying SMS codes will be removed as a two-factor option in March 2027. Does anyone know why? Our whole support team uses text codes and half of them don't have an authenticator app installed. We're on Starter, if that matters.

**Reply by kwame_builds:**
From what I understand, it's about security. Text messages can be intercepted, and attackers can trick carriers into moving your number to a new SIM. Authenticator apps generate codes on the device itself, so there's nothing to hijack in transit.

chunks.heading: SMS 2FA going away
chunks.text:
Go to Account > Security > Two-factor and add an app before the cutoff so you aren't locked out.

**Reply by dana_ops:**
That makes sense, thanks. I'll walk the team through switching this week, since it sounds like a quick change in the Security tab.

chunks.heading: Device clock and E4012
chunks.text:
Posted by dana_k in Nimbus Sync Help

Sync keeps failing on my Windows laptop with E4012 and the client won't finish signing in. Internet is fine and my password works. Anyone seen this? Reply from marcoP

Check the clock on that machine. Nimbus Sync seems to reject the connection when the device time is far off from real time. Mine had drifted after I swapped the battery in an old desktop. Look at the taskbar and compare with a phone. Reply from dana_k

That was it, thanks! My clock was set manually and was wrong.

chunks.heading: Device clock and E4012
chunks.text: I opened Settings, went to Time & language, then Date & time, and turned on Set time automatically. After that I restarted Nimbus Sync, and E4012 was gone. The sync folder started catching up right away. Hope this helps the next person who finds this thread.
